newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's DAX tumbles four percent at bourse start.
newsitem.headline: Germany's DAX tumbles four percent at bourse start.

text.p: Germany's DAX index, playing catch-up to Friday's severe losses on Wall Street, tumbled about four percent at the outset of bourse dealings as some traders said the market may have found a temporary bottom.
The 30-share DAX was down 167.30 points at 3,985.56 points. The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer trade, was down 84.14 points at 3,993.45 points.
"I think we have seen the worst for the day," said one Frankfurt dealer. "The selling is not a fresh wave but catching up to what happened on Friday after our bourse close."
Dealers, however, were concerned that the DAX was trading below 4,000 points and said it would be a psychological boost for the index to close above that level.

But they also said Germany's low interest rate environment, even with the threat of the Bundesbank nudging up rates in the near-term, and prospects for higher corporate earnings may prompt the German market to break away from the U.S. market if Wall Street falls to fresh losses.

"We have to remember that the DAX has been a real performer this year and it was time for some sort of a correction," said a Frankfurt dealer, noting the DAX has risen 55 percent since January compared with about 30 percent for the Dow Jones index.
"But the market appears to still be intact and the outlook remains optimistic," he said.
Trading volumes were heavy as top DAX components, including many export-senstive shares that posted hefty gains as the dollar surged toward 1.90 marks, were hit for hefty losses.

Among those lower were luxury carmaker Porsche AG, which fell 170 marks to 2,370 marks, and Volkswagen AG, which fell 49 marks to 1,243.00 marks ahead of its half-year results due out later on Monday.
Banking shares, propped up recently by speculation for a wave of mergers and takeovers, posted among the worst losses.
Commerzbank AG, considered a top takeover candidate, was down four at 62.10 marks and Deutsche Bank AG was down 5.80 marks at 109.00 marks.
BHF Bank, also considered to be a top takeover target, was among the top percentage loss leaders, as was Bankgesellschaft Berlin.
BHF fell 2.05 marks to 53.00 marks, while Bankgesellschaft Berlin slumped 5.25 marks to 43.25 marks.
Among those bucking the losses was television network ProSieben AG, whose preference shares were up one mark at 85.50 marks.
